title: Why CoT Monitoring Wins on Subtle but Loses on Obvious Sabotage

original_idea.body:
# Why CoT Monitoring Wins on Subtle but Loses on Obvious Sabotage

**Problem:** CoT Red-Handed found CoT monitoring beats action-only monitoring by 30+ points on subtle side tasks but can do WORSE on obvious sabotage because reasoning traces contain misleading rationalizations. The mechanism behind this crossover is unexplained.

**Direction:** Using the public CoT Red-Handed / ControlArena task transcripts (or regenerating a small slice via API), bucket sabotage attempts by 'subtlety' (e.g. number of action steps, how localized the harmful edit is) and plot monitor catch-rate vs. subtlety for CoT vs action-only. Hand-code a sample of cases where CoT monitoring underperforms to identify whether 'innocent-sounding rationalization' is the dominant failure category.

**Why it matters:** Knowing exactly when CoT helps vs hurts lets deployers pick a monitoring mode per task type. This is doable entirely outside a lab with open transcripts and a cheap trusted-monitor model, and addresses a near-term diffuse-reward monitoring problem labs underinvest in.

**Relevant context:** CoT Red-Handed (arXiv:2505.23575): action-only monitoring <20% catch rate on subtle side tasks; CoT improves by >30pp; but reasoning traces with misleading rationalizations reduce CoT performance on obvious sabotage. Hybrid weighted protocol doubles detection vs action-only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: explaining the CoT crossover lets deployers pick monitoring mode per task type.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Bucket transcripts by subtlety, plot catch-rate, hand-code failures; accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused catch-rate-vs-subtlety analysis plus qualitative coding, a few moving parts.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Diffuse-reward monitoring problem labs underinvest in, public transcripts.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only scoring on transcripts, free-tier feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Crossover observed; the mechanism explanation may be open.
